title: Daisey Martin and her Jazz Bellhops and four OKeh records
summary: He rehearsed with Daisey Martin's group in bellhop uniforms and made about four records for OKeh in 1920, after Mamie Smith's first sides.

bands.name: Daisey Martin and her Jazz Bellhops

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: That was my first trip on -- actually on the stage outside of the circus, with a platform, more or less. And, then I met -- they said for me to come rehearse with another group called Daisey Martin and her Jazz Bellhops.
Well, how did they get Jazz Bellhops? Were they actually bellhops, or --
No, no. We had bellhop uniforms on, you know, the red --
Remember Johnny for Phillip Morris? The uniform --
Same only red. And we made about four records on OKeh.

This must have been 1920. 1920. Because Mamie Smith had made her "Right Here for You" and "Crazy Blues" -- I didn't make that with Mamie. A "Good Man is Hard to Find" -- yeah. I made "Right Here for You" and "Crazy Blues", but she had already had two sides out in 1920, being the first Negro woman to sing on record -- the first blues --
